chapter: New York dance bands and Dorsey
title: Sy Oliver renews Dorsey; bandleaders as institutions
summary: Freeman says Sy Oliver's arrangements gave Dorsey new life and that Lombardo, Herman, Goodman and Miller are institutions.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: Yes. But the thing is that Sy, I think -- it's difficult to say, but I think Sy's arrangements gave Tommy a whole new life.
Maybe he kept him going, and it's difficult to say because Tommy's name was already established and he liked Guy Lombardo.
You see, once a thing was established in the dance music field, there was not -- that was it, you were there and you were there to stay.
If Lombardo had lived to be 1000 his music would still have sold.
Sure and he wouldn't have altered it.

He would be an institution. Take the case of Woody Herman today, he's an institution. He can go on as long as he wants to work. Because he's done it. He has done a great job. He's a lovely guy and he is marvelous -- I saw him the other night on unintelligible show here. He's an institution.
Benny Goodman is an institution. Tommy Dorsey, Glenn Miller, they are institutions. So it didn't make much difference what they did, but I think that Sy Oliver gave Tommy a whole new life.
